newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.

text.p: ASC CLAIMS A$210 MILLION FROM TRUSTEE COMPANY
The Australian Securities Commission is seeking up to A$210 million compensation in what's said to be its biggest case in New South Wales.
The ASC alleges Permanent Trustee Australia made an unauthorised investment and conducted a speculative and hazardous investment between April 1988 and December 1990.
The Commission is taking action on behalf of 23-thousand investors, alleging they lost A$145 million.
The hearing, underway in the Supreme Court in Sydney involves about 27 barristers, and their instructing solicitors.
HOWARD REJECTS HANSON VIEW ON AID
The Prime Minister has rejected a call from Independent M-P Pauline Hanson for cuts to foreign aid. Mr Howard has replied to a question in Parliament from Ms Hanson.

He says he understands the anger of Australians who believe spending on foreign aid is wasted but it's a short-sighted view. Mr Howard says there's an obligation on Government to make certain aid is efficiently directed, and political pressure is brought to bear on countries with intolerable regimes.
Mr Howard also says there's a national interest for Australia in foreign aid, for example in ensuring the stability of Papua New Guinea.
NSW PROTEST OF EAST TIMOR RIGHTS
In New South Wales, pro-democracy activists for East Timor have finished a 24 hour hunger strike in Newcastle as part of an International Day of protest.
The Maritime Union is also taking part in the day, with members delaying the two Indonesian ships at Port.
Union official Laurie Stein says the protest aims to express support for human rights in Indonesia, and independence for East Timor.
The International day of protest is calling on the Indonesian Government to release more than 30 activists who've been charged with subversion.
SMALL MONOPOLIES STIFLING PORTS
Australia's port industry has been warned the country will never achieve world class status while many ports are run by small monopolies.

The president of the Australian Ports and Marine Authorities Association, Peter Morgan, told a national conference in Hobart today that greater sharing of facilities and multi-skilling was essential if the industry were to improve.
Mr Morgan said it was virtually impossible for the industry and Australia to benefit while ports had separate stevedores, tugs, pilots and linesmen working alone for different owners.

He said the secret of port efficiency was to minimise idle time. Mr Morgan says that could best be done if individual operators allowed workers with free time to help other operators or to take part in general port maintenance.
OLYMPIC SOCCER BID LAUNCHED
Canberra has launched its bid to get a share of the Sydney 2000 Olympics .... as host of Olympic soccer matches at Bruce Stadium.
The Sydney Organising Committee will be in Canberra on Wednesday to inspect facilities before watching the international between Australia and Tahiti on Friday night...
Meanwhile ACT Soccer president Steve Dospot has called on Australian selectors to include local player Paul Wade in the Socceroos lineup.
RECORD BREAKING JOCKEY TO MISS MELBOURNE CUP

The world's most famous jockey looks set to miss the Melbourne Cup. Frankie Dettori, who created headlines earlier this month by riding seven winners in a day at Royal Ascot, was to have ridden Grey Shot in the Cup. But Dettori is staying home to honour a contract with owner, Sheikh Mohammed ... with Pat Eddery likely to take the Cup ride. In other racing news .... Trainer Bart Cummings has accepted an invitation for Cox Plate winner Saintly to run in the Japan Cup. Cummings says he received the invitation by phone this morning, and says Saintly will head to Japan some time after the Melbourne Cup. Octagonal has also been invited to Japan to contest the A$5 million event.
-- Reuters Sydney newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
